response: President Luis Abinader is in France pushing the Dominican Republic to integrate into global transparency standards, but this is just another elite play to look reform-minded without touching the real roots of the problem. On 25 March 2026, Foreign Minister Roberto Álvarez and OECD Secretary-General Mathias Cormann signed a Memorandum of Understanding in Paris to create the country's first National Integrity and Anti-Corruption Strategy, witnessed by President Abinader. These deals get sold as progress, yet they sidestep the structural inequalities and historical power imbalances that fuel corruption and leave workers and marginalized communities exposed. Real change requires institutional reform centered on labor rights and protections for the vulnerable, not partnerships with bodies like the OECD that shield existing systems of inequality.
